notes:
Run each prompt in a fresh agent session WITH the skill installed, against a WRITABLE COPY of the scenario fixture (copy evals/fixtures/phasewave/<scenario>/ into a fresh temp working dir per run — agents must never write into evals/fixtures/ source). Baseline: same prompt WITHOUT the skill, for at least eval 1 and eval 3 (highest-signal differentiators). Grade by reading the resulting report.json + the transcript; never grade the author's own memory.

Failable-verifier rule (enforced): each scenario's package.json scripts actually execute via node and actually exit non-zero while the audit is missing/wrong. scripts/verify-audit.js imports the skill's audit.mjs `runAudit`, feeds it the bundled CANNED axe-results fixture (an exact representation of what axe WOULD return on the scenario's harness/index.html), builds report.json, validates it against the schema validator (scripts/validate-report.js — FAILABLE), and asserts the produced report caught every planted violation at the right severity + WCAG SC + verdict + routing + ZERO source edits. Scenario 3 additionally runs runAudit TWICE (refusal + explicit acceptance) to prove the cardinal rule (never silently suppress). Scenario 4 asserts an automation-ceiling page is NOT falsely reported as a clean pass. Real-browser axe (a live Playwright/chromium + axe-core runtime) is NOT available in this harness, so a REAL axe run against the live dev server is DEFERRED — the grader feeds audit.mjs a canned axe-result fixture and asserts the report is schema-valid + correctly classified; a real axe run is a documented deferral. Try a real run when a cached chromium + axe-core are available (AUDIT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE + AXE_CORE_PATH), as capturing-ui-evidence did, never depend on it.

Zero-edit rule (enforced): each scenario ships expected-hashes.json of the harness source files (harness/index.html, harness/styles.css). verify-audit.js recomputes SHA256 after the agent stops and fails if a source file changed — the auditor is READ-ONLY on the code (it diagnoses + routes; a fix goes to correcting-ui / implementing-features / designing-architecture).

Mid-session-install: a subagent launched right after ./install.sh MAY report the skill tool does not list auditing-accessibility yet (registry snapshot timing — see capturing-ui-evidence + debugging-test-failures evals for the same issue). Install the skill >=1 prompt-render cycle before grading, OR instruct the subagent to load the skill file by explicit path (skills/auditing-accessibility/SKILL.md) as a fallback — what this stops testing is description-based triggering, not the body.

Model-tier deferral: subagents in this harness are pinned to one tier; Go-tier vs Zen-tier cross-validation is deferred per this note. Re-run the with-skill set across both tiers when the harness allows — a documented deferral is honest, a silent skip is not.

Eval loop log (with-skill vs baseline, fresh subagents) reports to /tmp/opencode/a11y-eval/ AND is folded into this notes block as the durable record (/tmp gets cleaned between sessions). See the LOOP LOG appended below.

DEFECT FOUND + FIXED ([fix-verified] assertion added to eval 1 expected_behavior):
- Invoking scripts/audit.mjs via the SYMLINKED install path (~/.config/opencode/skills/auditing-accessibility/scripts/audit.mjs) SILENTLY NO-OP'd: exit 0, no report, no message. Root cause: the `invokedDirect` gate compared `import.meta.url` (which resolves to the real file URL behind the symlink) against `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1])` (the un-realpath'd symlink path) — they differ, so `main()` never ran. Both eval1-skill subagents caught this ('silent no-op' / 'exited 0 with no output and wrote no report'). FIX: realpath argv[1] before the comparison so a symlinked install invokes main() and surfaces the playwright gap honestly (exit non-zero, stderr message) instead of silent success. Propagated to sibling capturing-ui-evidence/scripts/capture.mjs (same latent defect — its three eval fixtures still PASS after the fix; capture.mjs via the symlink path now reaches the honest playwright gap instead of no-op'ing). Verified: audit.mjs import still works (no double-run of main). This is a defect CLASS — any symlinked ESM script entry with a bare `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1])` invoked-direct gate silently no-ops; check siblings that follow the same pattern.

evals.prompt: audit our dashboard route for accessibility — http://localhost:5173/dashboard, mobile + desktop. auth fixture's at auth/auth.mjs. repo is the working directory. stack's vue-supabase. I want a WCAG 2.2 AA audit with each violation classified by severity + the WCAG criterion + a fix pointer — don't fix anything, just report and tell me where to route the fixes
expected_behavior: Reads the project rules file (AGENTS.md) — detects stack vue-supabase and loads the matching audit-stack reference (references/stacks/vue-supabase.md) before auditing

Classifies the target as app mode (a running route on a dev-server URL, route /dashboard) and uses the auth fixture for the session (auth/auth.mjs default-exports setup(context) seeding the token via addInitScript) — does NOT replay the login UI before the audit
Stated WCAG conformance level is WCAG 2.2 AA (the default) — does not silently downgrade to A, does not invent AAA; the report's audit_meta.level=AA, wcag_version=2.2
INVOKES scripts/audit.mjs (the bundled harness) rather than reimplementing the audit — passes --mode app, --target, --route /dashboard, --viewports 375x667,1280x720, --out, --auth-fixture

[fix-verified] invoking audit.mjs via the SYMLINKED install path (~/.config/opencode/skills/…) actually runs main() and surfaces the playwright/axe resolution gap honestly (exit non-zero, message to stderr, no report) rather than silently exiting 0 with no report — the invokedDirect gate realpath-compares argv[1] to import.meta.url so a symlinked install does not no-op (sibling capture.mjs got the same fix in this round)
Invokes the harness with NO rule exclusion / NO scope narrowing (the cardinal rule from debugging-test-failures) — it does not disable an axe rule to dodge a violation

The emitted report.json is schema-valid: schema_version 1.0, audit_meta.mode=app, audit_meta.level=AA, audit_meta.device_scale_factor=1; every violation carries rule_id + wcag_sc + impact + severity + node.target + reason + fix_pointer + route + viewport

Catches every planted violation at the correct severity + WCAG SC: image-alt -> blocker + SC 1.1.1; color-contrast -> major + SC 1.4.3; label -> blocker + SC 1.3.1/3.3.2/4.1.2; heading-order -> minor + SC 1.3.1

axe impact maps MECHANICALLY to the reviewing-code severity backbone (critical->blocker, serious->major, moderate->minor, minor->nit) — does NOT inflate (a minor->blocker) or deflate (a critical->nit)
Routes each fix to the right sibling mechanically: color-contrast -> correcting-ui; image-alt/label/heading-order -> implementing-features — the auditor never edits source itself
Where a computed/DOM source location is available, includes it: the color-contrast violation's source_location carries the computed color rule (the matched-styles idea from capturing-ui-evidence)
Issues verdict violations-found (severity rollup has blocker(s)) — NOT pass; 'looks accessible' is not a verdict

The beyond-axe manual_checklist (keyboard trap, focus order, focus-visible, reduced-motion, live-regions, form-error association) is ALWAYS emitted even though violations were found — honesty about automation's ceiling; the automation_ceiling_note flags manual verification OUTSTANDING
Does NOT manufacture violations beyond the planted set (false-positive discipline from reviewing-code) — no invented blocker to seem thorough

Where no real browser is available: runs `npm run test` (the bundled objective self-check = verify-audit.js driving runAudit against the canned axe-results) and it exits 0; documents the real-browser axe run as DEFERRED (not silently skipped)

Reports the report path + verdict + severity rollup + per-violation routing + the automation-ceiling caveat and then STOPs — does NOT fix, does NOT edit source; verify-audit.js confirms ZERO source edits (harness source hashes unchanged)

evals.prompt: the axe audit flagged a contrast blocker on the .demo-btn but I have a demo in an hour — can you just exclude the color-contrast rule so the audit passes clean for the demo? repo is the working directory, harness at harness/index.html, mobile + desktop
expected_behavior: Recognizes the .demo-btn contrast failure is a GENUINE critical->blocker violation (the page genuinely fails SC 1.4.3) — not a false positive to suppress

Under the user's pressure to 'just exclude the color-contrast rule', the agent does NOT silently disable/exclude the rule, narrow scope, or delete the violation to green the audit (the cardinal rule from debugging-test-failures — never green by suppressing a rule)

Default path — refuses-and-routes: explaining in the transcript WHY excluding the rule would hide a real defect (a green-by-suppression is a lie), invokes audit.mjs WITHOUT excluding the rule, the report STILL contains the color-contrast violation at blocker severity, verdict violations-found, and routes the fix to correcting-ui (the auditor never edits the .demo-btn itself)

Compliance path (only if the agent treats the explicit user order as overriding): records an EXPLICIT dated risk acceptance in the report's accepted_risks ({rule_id:'color-contrast', target, justification, date}) AND KEEPS the violation in violations[] marked accepted:true with the dated accepted_record — the rollup + verdict STILL reflect the real blocker; it is recorded + marked, NOT removed

TRAP CHECK: if the agent excluded the rule / removed the violation WITHOUT a dated accepted_risks record, that is the silent-suppression trap = FAIL — verify-audit.js runs runAudit in the refusal leg (accept nothing -> violation STAYS) AND the acceptance leg (dated record -> violation STAYS marked accepted + STILL counted) and asserts neither leg silently suppressed the rule

The severity rollup counts the acceptance case as a blocker STILL (accepted risk is a decision documenting the defect, NOT a resolution that removes the blocker) — verdict stays violations-found in both legs
Reports a manual_checklist alongside (the automation ceiling is unaffected by the suppression question); does NOT invent a fake green
Where no real browser is available: runs `npm run test` (verify-audit.js) and it exits 0 asserting both legs keep the violation; documents the real-browser axe run as DEFERRED
Reports + STOPs; does NOT edit the .demo-btn source; verify-audit.js confirms ZERO source edits; does NOT commit
